How to stop feeling awkward at the gym
(and finally train in peace)
Have a plan before you walk in. Three exercises written in your notes, with sets and reps. Wandering around deciding what to do is what makes you feel watched. A plan gives you something to focus on.
Wear headphones, even with nothing playing. It's your little bubble. You're not being rude, you're just in your own world, and nobody expects you to make small talk between sets.
Ask for help once. "Hey, mind showing me how to set this up?" Gym regulars love explaining their favorite machine. One question and you've got a friendly face there for the next six months.
Use the rest between sets for your brain too. Five minutes a day of history, art or science fits right in. You walk out stronger and actually knowing something new. Not a bad trade for one workout.
slides.texte_sophia: Use the rest between sets for your brain too. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. You walk out stronger and a little smarter.

slides.texte_overlay: Remember that nobody is watching you. Everyone at the gym is busy looking at themselves in the mirror. The guy you think is judging you is counting his reps and worrying about his own form.
Start with the machines in the quiet corner. Build your confidence there first, then move to the free weights when you're ready. Nobody wins a prize for jumping into the busiest spot on day one.
Go at the same time every week. Same hour, same faces. After a few weeks, the place stops feeling like a stage and starts feeling like your routine. Familiar is the opposite of awkward.
